Definition: Seeing or hearing peers take medicine can trigger one's own routine.
Subtheme: Care work and reminders circulate through relationships and presence
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "They don't tell me take yours. They say I have to take mine and then I remember mine. Same thing." (P04, Phase 1, L107)
Reflexivity_note: I separated incidental cues from explicit family checking.
Interview_gap: Incidental peer cueing is distinct from explicit family monitoring; retain as contextual support, not a central mechanism.

Definition: Whoever is nearby may remind, so responsibility moves with household presence.
Subtheme: Care work and reminders circulate through relationships and presence
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "Whoever is around. It depends on who is at home." (P02, Phase 1, L377)
Reflexivity_note: This is circulation, not evidence that nobody carries primary responsibility.

Definition: Families discuss options, but participants reserve medication changes for clinicians.
Subtheme: Knowledge, interpretation, supply, and clinical authority sit with different people
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "No no. Change means doctor has to say." (P06, Phase 1, L103)
Reflexivity_note: Peer influence does not erase the consistently stated clinical boundary.

Definition: Kin retain papers and translate clinical instructions into household routines.
Subtheme: Knowledge, interpretation, supply, and clinical authority sit with different people
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "My son. He keeps the prescription also. He knows what doctor said." (P04, Phase 1, L51)
Reflexivity_note: The evidence names several kin roles, so I did not reduce this to one caregiver.

Definition: Pharmacists translate difficult prescriptions and identify medicines without taking prescribing authority.
Subtheme: Knowledge, interpretation, supply, and clinical authority sit with different people
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "Pharmacy person can understand it. We cannot understand properly. So we ask them."
Reflexivity_note: I retained pharmacists because the care network extends beyond co residents.

Code: Shared-device access makes digital participation relational
Definition: Some older adults access phones through family-owned or family-configured devices, making proxy use part of ordinary participation rather than an exceptional fallback.
Subtheme: Knowledge, interpretation, supply, and clinical authority sit with different people
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "My son has one... If I need to talk I use his phone." (P06, Phase 1, L59)
Reflexivity_note: Shared access should not be coded as absence of agency; it changes who performs setup and interaction work.
Interview_gap: Device ownership and sharing were not demonstrated consistently across all interviews; avoid prevalence claims.

Definition: Repeated positive accounts from family, friends, or peers can increase confidence in a medicine while participants still distinguish that influence from clinical authorization.
Subtheme: Knowledge, interpretation, supply, and clinical authority sit with different people
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "Many people saying same thing I listen more." (P12, Phase 1, L85)
Reflexivity_note: The interviews repeatedly prompted group-opinion hypotheticals; retain as contextual evidence but do not make it a headline finding.
Interview_gap: Some group-influence questions were leading and repeated; use only to bound trust/authority claims.

Definition: Some older adults reject assistance or technology as unnecessary for current routines.
Subtheme: Older adults preserve practical agency through routine, recognition, and selective independence
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "Yes, my memory is very sharp." (P17, Phase 1, L27)
Reflexivity_note: The claim performs competence and also reports a practice; both readings remain.

Definition: Familiar packaging supports action without recall of biomedical names.
Subtheme: Older adults preserve practical agency through routine, recognition, and selective independence
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "I can tell which one I take because I see it every day. But the name I cannot say." (P03, Phase 1, L71)
Reflexivity_note: Visual recognition is competence here, not a lesser substitute for reading.

Code: Self-directed regimen adjustment is an under-probed boundary case
Definition: One older adult reported skipping medicines he considered unnecessary when unwell, complicating a simple claim that medication changes always remain with clinicians.
Subtheme: Older adults preserve practical agency through routine, recognition, and selective independence
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "Whenever health is not at an optimal level, I skip some medicines which are not required for that particular illness." (P17, Phase 1, L43)
Reflexivity_note: Do not interpret this as clinically appropriate behavior; analytically it is a boundary case about self-directed authority.
Interview_gap: The interviewer did not ask which medicines, how often, whether the doctor knew, or how the participant decided; keep strictly as a boundary case.

Definition: Older adults may retain dosing while kin handle identification, supply, or interpretation.
Subtheme: Older adults preserve practical agency through routine, recognition, and selective independence
Theme: Medication work is relationally distributed, while agency and authority remain differentiated
Example_quote: "Taking is easy. Knowing which medicine is little difficult" (P08, Phase 1, L101)
Reflexivity_note: I separated taking from knowing to avoid treating distributed work as dependence.

Definition: Frequent questions can feel irritating even when later interpreted as help.
Subtheme: Checking carries care, worry, and relational pressure at the same time
Theme: Breakdowns emerge at routine and handoff boundaries, creating uncertainty, burden, and adherence risk
Example_quote: "Sometimes I get irritated also because she asks so much. But later I think okay she is helping." (P05, Phase 1, L223)
Reflexivity_note: This prevents checking from being coded as either care or surveillance in advance.
Interview_gap: Older-adult response to checking was inconsistently probed; preserve as counterevidence to treating monitoring as automatically benign.

Definition: Shared reminding can fail when all available people are occupied simultaneously.
Subtheme: Routine transitions separate medicines, cues, people, and dose times
Theme: Breakdowns emerge at routine and handoff boundaries, creating uncertainty, burden, and adherence risk
Example_quote: "No family was there. But everybody was busy. Nobody remembered either." (P13, Phase 1, L53)
Reflexivity_note: This supports collective lapse, but no household pairing is available.

Definition: Leaving home can separate a person from medicine even when timing is remembered.
Subtheme: Routine transitions separate medicines, cues, people, and dose times
Theme: Breakdowns emerge at routine and handoff boundaries, creating uncertainty, burden, and adherence risk
Example_quote: "When I go somewhere, sometimes I forget to carry the medicine." (P02, Phase 1, L173)
Reflexivity_note: I kept carrying separate from remembering because they require different designs.

Definition: Travel, guests, and altered meals remove the cues that ordinarily carry dosing.
Subtheme: Routine transitions separate medicines, cues, people, and dose times
Theme: Breakdowns emerge at routine and handoff boundaries, creating uncertainty, burden, and adherence risk
Example_quote: "At home, everything is fixed. I know where the medicine is, I know the time. When travelling, everything changes." (P01, Phase 1, L95)
Reflexivity_note: The mechanism is cue displacement, not a global memory deficit.

Definition: Farming, housework, and paid work reorganize attention around tasks rather than dose times.
Subtheme: Routine transitions separate medicines, cues, people, and dose times
Theme: Breakdowns emerge at routine and handoff boundaries, creating uncertainty, burden, and adherence risk
Example_quote: "Farming work doesn't have fixed time always." (P06, Phase 1, L71)
Reflexivity_note: Different work settings share temporal instability, not identical burdens.

Definition: Changes in strip appearance, brand, company, or packaging can unsettle recognition built through familiar medicine identity.
Subtheme: Supply and medicine-identity changes create non-reminder failures
Theme: Breakdowns emerge at routine and handoff boundaries, creating uncertainty, burden, and adherence risk
Example_quote: "When doctor changes one medicine, the new strip looks different." (P07, Phase 1, L115)
Reflexivity_note: Visual cues help only while packaging remains stable.

Definition: A dose can be missed because medicine is depleted or locally unavailable, even when timing is remembered.
Subtheme: Supply and medicine-identity changes create non-reminder failures
Theme: Breakdowns emerge at routine and handoff boundaries, creating uncertainty, burden, and adherence risk
Example_quote: "We forget to buy before it finishes. Then there is no medicine" (P08, Phase 1, L149)
Reflexivity_note: Supply failure widens the problem beyond reminder design.

Definition: A reminder should specify medicine, timing, dose, or relation to food.
Subtheme: Actionable prompts connect reminders to familiar medicine while respecting context
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "It should tell me clearly which medicine, how much, and when to take it."
Reflexivity_note: Specific content answers the failure of generic alarms, despite elicitation.
Interview_gap: Mostly elicited design expectation; distinguish from actual tool use.

Definition: Spoken reminders may need quieter modes when other people are present.
Subtheme: Actionable prompts connect reminders to familiar medicine while respecting context
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "If other people are around, I don't want everyone hearing my medicine reminder." (P02, Phase 1, L277)
Reflexivity_note: This single case complicates any universal voice first recommendation.
Interview_gap: Single P02 case; useful as a countercase to universal voice-first design.

Definition: Pictures and simple time cues connect digital instructions to familiar medicine appearance.
Subtheme: Actionable prompts connect reminders to familiar medicine while respecting context
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "If I see the photo I know. This is the one." (P04, Phase 1, L171)
Reflexivity_note: Packaging changes limit this mechanism, so images cannot stand alone.
Interview_gap: Pictures can support matching but packaging changes make image-only identification brittle.

Definition: Spoken reminders can be noticed without opening or reading a screen.
Subtheme: Actionable prompts connect reminders to familiar medicine while respecting context
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "I don't have to look at the phone. I can just hear it." (P02, Phase 1, L273)
Reflexivity_note: Preference was often elicited after voice was proposed by the interviewer.
Interview_gap: Voice preference was frequently elicited after voice was proposed; report as evaluated preference, not spontaneous demand.

Definition: Technology should complement relational care rather than replace family and community roles.
Subtheme: Delegated setup can support use, but accountable people retain authority
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "we don't live in isolation. My family ensures my medicine stock is full [...] Technology should complement that" (P10, Phase 1, L84)
Reflexivity_note: This direct account supports relational interdependence, while independent managers bound its reach.
Interview_gap: Supports relational interdependence while independent self-managers bound its reach.

Definition: Trusted kin may enter schedules while older adults retain everyday use.
Subtheme: Delegated setup can support use, but accountable people retain authority
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "Son or wife. They should put the medicine. I can only take when it tells me." (P06, Phase 1, L263)
Reflexivity_note: Delegation can support participation, but setup authority still needs revocability.
Interview_gap: Settings-control questions were inconsistently asked; retain as formative design evidence, not a prevalence claim.

Definition: Technology may inform or warn but should not recommend medication changes.
Subtheme: Delegated setup can support use, but accountable people retain authority
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "We listen to both. But medicine doctor decides."
Reflexivity_note: This boundary is strongly corroborated despite hypothetical prompting.
Interview_gap: Strongly aligned with multiple accounts, but future-system statements are design judgments.

Definition: Trust rises when kin or professionals check system information against the prescription.
Subtheme: Delegated setup can support use, but accountable people retain authority
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "If son puts everything then I will trust it more. I know he checked it." (P04, Phase 1, L179)
Reflexivity_note: Trust attaches to accountable people rather than the system alone.
Interview_gap: Trust is described through accountable people; this should not be converted into a claim that users distrust automation generally.

Definition: Multi step interaction prompts users to stop or delegate.
Subtheme: Device, document, and interaction conditions shape who can participate directly
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "I press wrong thing and something else comes. Then I leave it." (P06, Phase 1, L167)
Reflexivity_note: I coded withdrawal as patterned participation, not failed adoption.

Definition: Button phones, shared phones, or limited device ownership can narrow direct interaction and move some digital work to kin.
Subtheme: Device, document, and interaction conditions shape who can participate directly
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "I only know how to press the green button when it rings to talk" (P09, Phase 1, L62)
Reflexivity_note: This is an infrastructural condition, not an age based incapacity.

Definition: Small labels and handwritten prescriptions require glasses or another reader.
Subtheme: Device, document, and interaction conditions shape who can participate directly
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "Big letters yes. Small letters no. I need glasses. Without glasses I can see the packet but not the writing." (P03, Phase 1, L75)
Reflexivity_note: Reading barriers vary, so voice cannot be treated as universally preferred.

Definition: Missing a button press should not be treated as missing medication.
Subtheme: Escalation should be delayed, selective, visible, and epistemically modest
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Evidence_status: Design judgment grounded in lived practice
Example_quote: "Taking medicine is the main thing. Pressing button should be secondary." (P05, Phase 1, L211)
Reflexivity_note: This exposes a gap between recorded interaction and lived action.
Interview_gap: Important epistemic boundary: interface confirmation and medication ingestion are not equivalent.

Definition: Caregivers should receive meaningful exceptions, not every reminder event.
Subtheme: Escalation should be delayed, selective, visible, and epistemically modest
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "But not for every small thing. If I really don't take it, then maybe family can know." (P01, Phase 1, L211)
Reflexivity_note: A real miss remains technically uncertain without verified sensing or logs.
Interview_gap: Hypothetical preference; a non-confirmation cannot establish a missed dose.

Definition: Families prefer another reminder and time to respond before involving someone else.
Subtheme: Escalation should be delayed, selective, visible, and epistemically modest
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "Maybe after some minutes... Then another reminder. But not every one minute."
Reflexivity_note: The sequence was prompted, so it is an evaluated expectation, not observed practice.

Definition: A generic sound may not identify which medicine or action is due.
Subtheme: Existing aids can create work or signal without completing the handoff
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "Too much sound. I don't know which alarm is for what... sometimes I don't understand why it is ringing."
Reflexivity_note: The problem is underspecified content, not sound itself.
Interview_gap: Generic-alarm limitation is supported, but reminder designs were often discussed after interviewer prompting.

Definition: A reminder may be noticed yet deferred until it is forgotten.
Subtheme: Existing aids can create work or signal without completing the handoff
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "Alarm helps but if I am doing something then I may not take it immediately. Then after some time I remember." (P12, Phase 1, L29)
Reflexivity_note: This is one user's lived alarm practice and bounds reminder efficacy claims.
Interview_gap: P12 provides direct lived use showing that noticing a reminder is not equivalent to taking a dose.

Definition: Some self managers see no present need for medication technology.
Subtheme: Low-technology practices and refusal remain legitimate baselines
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "Yes, absolutely, I do not need those yet." (P11, Phase 1, L35)
Reflexivity_note: Need is contingent on regimen and context, not age alone.
Interview_gap: Explicit refusal/self-sufficiency is analytically important and should remain visible in results.

Definition: Notes, prescriptions, labels, and leaflets can organize complex medication schedules.
Subtheme: Low-technology practices and refusal remain legitimate baselines
Theme: Technology is legitimate when it repairs bounded coordination gaps without displacing situated competence or human authority
Example_quote: "I have them noted down. Husband also notes for me, I take them according to that." (P16, Phase 1, L15)
Reflexivity_note: This contradicts the former claim that nothing is written down.
